title: Route 66 Turns 100: America's Most Famous Road
summary:
America's famous road turned 100 years old. Route 66 was built in 1926. It runs from Chicago to Santa Monica, California — more than 2,000 miles through eight states.

Writer John Steinbeck gave the road its nickname, 'the Mother Road.' His 1939 book The Grapes of Wrath told the story of families driving west on Route 66 during the Dust Bowl, when dust storms in the 1930s pushed families off their farms. The book won a Pulitzer Prize.

The road has a song and a screen life, too. Bobby Troup wrote '(Get Your Kicks on) Route 66' in 1946, and Nat King Cole made it a hit. A TV show called Route 66 followed two friends driving across America, the 1969 movie Easy Rider sent three travelers down the road on motorcycles, and Pixar's 2006 movie Cars told its story in Radiator Springs, a town on Route 66.

The road stopped being a federal highway in 1985, but people love it. Route 66 expert Michael Wallis says the road is all about adventure — and a peek at a dream.
why_it_matters: A family road trip can turn into a real-life adventure, just like the stories, songs, and movies about Route 66 show.

background_read: Route 66 is a famous road that runs across America from Chicago to Santa Monica, California, passing through eight states.
Long ago, many families drove west on it to find new homes and work after dust storms pushed them off their farms.
Today people still love the road for its adventure, its small towns, and the songs and movies it inspired.

WHAT: A road built in 1926 marked its 100th birthday and is still celebrated in books, songs, a TV show, and movies.
WHERE: From Chicago to Santa Monica, California, running more than 2,000 miles through eight states.
WHY: People love the road because it stands for adventure and a peek at a dream, and its stories keep it famous even though it stopped being a federal highway in 1985.
